findings.headline: Significant deferrals across Subject to Appraisal projects, with £6.25m of £8.4m budget removed from 2026/27 forecast
findings.detail: The Subject to Appraisal section originally budgeted £8.4m but only £1.6m is now forecast for 2026/27, representing £6.25m of deferrals. Major deferrals include: leisure centre demolition (£2m), LEP applications (£2m), CWR CIL infrastructure (£1m), and Brooks car park air handling unit works (£1m). Projects are being pushed into 2027/28 or pending approval.
findings.matters: Substantial deferrals in capital programme create uncertainty about timing of capital expenditure and may indicate spending constraints or delayed project readiness
findings.figures: Subject to Appraisal original budget £8,415k, other changes -£6,250k, forecast £1,580k
findings.quote: Now expected in 2027/28

findings.headline: River Park leisure centre demolition deferred from 2026/27 and budget reduced following costings
findings.detail: The leisure centre demolition was a £2m Subject to Appraisal project for 2026/27 that has now been completely removed from this year's forecast and reprofiled to 2027/28. The council notes that the budget has been reduced following costings, indicating either cost pressures or scope adjustments have emerged.
findings.matters: Material capital project deferrals and budget reductions indicate either cost pressures or execution delays on major projects, affecting cash flow and borrowing needs
findings.figures: £2,000k originally budgeted, now £0 forecast for 2026/27
findings.quote: Reprofiled to 27/28 and budget reduced following costings

findings.headline: Sewage treatment works budget of £0.4m insufficient for four planned upgrades; only three will proceed
findings.detail: The Cabinet had set aside £0.4m for sewage site upgrade works to reduce running costs and reduce HRA subsidy to treatment sites. Following initial feasibility work, the council now estimates this budget will only fund three plant upgrades rather than the originally intended four. Additional budget requests will be made as business cases are developed for the fourth site.
findings.matters: Insufficient budget to complete planned maintenance works suggests either cost underestimation or delayed delivery of planned efficiency improvements that would reduce ongoing HRA operating subsidy requirements.
findings.figures: £0.4m budget, originally intended for four site upgrades, now sufficient for three upgrades only
findings.quote: Note that the £0.4m for sewerage site upgrade works set by Cabinet at its meeting of September 2024 is now only sufficient to fund three plant upgrades, rather than the originally intended four, and that additional budget requests will be made as business cases are developed.

findings.headline: Right to Buy sales spiked to 33 properties in 2025/26, significantly above historic average but expected to decline
findings.detail: The council sold 33 properties under Right to Buy in 2025/26, significantly higher than historic average and higher than the increased budget assumption. The council notes that changes to the RTB scheme implemented in late 2024/25 "make the scheme significantly less attractive" and sales are expected to reduce in future years. The spike and subsequent decline will affect both housing stock numbers and rental income.
findings.matters: Material RTB sales volatility affects the council's housing stock base, rental income trajectory, and the availability of RTB 1-4-1 receipts for reinvestment in new affordable housing, which is a key council priority.
findings.figures: 33 RTB sales in 2025/26, adverse income variance £0.398m partially attributable to RTB sales and void properties
findings.quote: Thirty three properties were sold under right to buy in 2025/26, which is significantly higher than historic average.

findings.headline: Climate change retrofit programme £3.262m underspend; delivery strategy underwent redesign following delays
findings.detail: The climate change emergency budget of £5.336m in 2025/26 spent only £2.074m, a £3.26m underspend (61%). Delays in fabric works were caused by SHF Wave 3 documentation requirements and DESNZ holding battery installations. The SHF funding was rescinded, impacting construction schedules. The team redesigned the retrofit delivery strategy and piloted two new contractors. Underspent budget is being reprofiled to 2026-27 and beyond.
findings.matters: The programme restructuring and substantial slippage (61% underspend) raise delivery risk on the council's commitment to achieve EPC-C ratings on all stock by 2030, a key climate/energy performance objective.
findings.figures: Revised budget £5.336m, outturn £2.074m, variance £3.262m, £0.345m carried forward to 2026/27 for Swedish Cottages insulation pilots
findings.quote: The SHF funding was rescinded, which took time and impacted on the construction contract programme of works.

findings.headline: Fire safety capital programme £2.7m underspend; works reprofiled to 2026-27 and 2027-28
findings.detail: The fire safety provision budget of £3.551m for 2025/26 spent only £0.781m, resulting in a £2.7m underspend. The council prioritised high-risk fire safety measures (completed as revenue repairs) and immediate legislative compliance. A formal compartmentation and fire stopping programme commenced in Q4 2025/26, with the budget underspend being reprofiled to future years.
findings.matters: A 76% underspend on fire safety works suggests delivery challenges on a material capital programme, raising questions about realistic timelines and programme management for the wider capital plan.
findings.figures: Revised budget £3.551m, outturn £0.781m, variance £2.7m, original budget £3.301m
findings.quote: The budget underspend will be reprofiled across 2026/27 and 2027/28.

findings.headline: Responsive repair costs increased £0.519m due to damp and mould repairs identified in stock surveys
findings.detail: Responsive maintenance expenditure was £0.519m over budget in 2025/26. The council attributes this to increased repair volumes for damp and mould, as well as proactive repairs identified through ongoing stock condition surveys where HHSRS (Housing Health and Safety Rating System) and other safety issues were discovered and addressed.
findings.matters: Increased damp and mould repairs across the stock suggest systemic property quality issues that could require significant future investment and may impact tenant health, satisfaction, and potential legal liability.
findings.figures: £0.519m adverse variance on responsive maintenance, previous year responsive maintenance budget £4.322m, budget £0 shown against original of nil
findings.quote: This is in part due to increased repairs for damp and mould, but also as a result of the ongoing stock condition surveys, whereby HHSRS and other repairs identified during the surveys have been dealt with proactively.

findings.headline: Void maintenance costs increased £1.294m due to 17% more terminations and higher per-void costs
findings.detail: The number of HRA terminations increased from 296 in 2024/25 to 346 in 2025/26 (a 17% increase), with longer average relet times (18.69 to 19.12 days). The average revenue cost per void rose from £7,770 to £8,815 (13.5% increase). This combination drove a £1.294m adverse variance on the voids budget, making it the largest single service overspend.
findings.matters: Higher void costs and turnover directly impact rental income and HRA expenditure, indicating either rising property degradation, housing market volatility, or tenant churn that could signal underlying service delivery issues.
findings.figures: 346 terminations vs 296 prior year (17% increase), relet time 19.12 days vs 18.69 days, cost per void £8,815 vs £7,770 (13.5% increase), £1.294m adverse variance
findings.quote: There was therefore a 17% increase in terminations. The average revenue cost per termination also increased from £7,770 to £8,815.

findings.headline: HRA general balance decreased from £15.951m to £13.689m, a £2.262m annual drawdown
findings.detail: The council ran a £2.262m deficit in 2025/26, which was £0.232m worse than the originally budgeted deficit of £2.030m. This reduced the HRA working balance from £15.951m to £13.689m. At this rate of deficit, the general reserve would be depleted within 6-7 years.
findings.matters: A lender needs to assess the long-term sustainability of the HRA and whether the council can continue to fund capital works and maintain services without relying on external borrowing or further reserve depletion.
findings.figures: £15.951m opening balance, £13.689m closing balance, £2.262m deficit, original budget £2.030m deficit
findings.quote: The 2025/26 outturn was a deficit to the HRA of £2.262m for 2025/26, compared to the originally budgeted deficit of £2.030m; an adverse movement of £0.232m.

findings.headline: Strategic Asset Purchase Scheme: £4,000k approved budget entirely undeployed with no purchases made
findings.detail: The council's Strategic Asset Purchase Scheme had a £4,000k allocation approved for 2025/26 but recorded zero expenditure. The only explanation offered is that 'No suitable purchases identified', with no detail on strategy, market constraints, or revised intentions.
findings.matters: A large capital allocation for strategic acquisitions remaining entirely undeployed signals either execution risk in the council's asset strategy or changed market circumstances a lender should understand.
findings.figures: £4,000k approved budget, £0 actual expenditure
findings.quote: No suitable purchases identified

findings.headline: £60k of revenue costs reclassified as capital for Chesil Theatre works
findings.detail: The council recorded £60k actual capital expenditure on Chesil Theatre with no approved budget. The comment explicitly states this was 'revenue spend identified as capital in nature', indicating costs that were revenue in character were recorded within the capital outturn.
findings.matters: Reclassification of revenue costs as capital obscures the council's true revenue budget position and may indicate weak expenditure controls.
findings.figures: £60k actual expenditure recorded as capital despite being revenue in nature
findings.quote: Revenue spend identified as capital in nature

findings.headline: Unbudgeted £91k capital expenditure for archaeology at St Clement's surgery replacement where prior year works created budget shortfall
findings.detail: The council recorded £91k of capital expenditure in 2025/26 on replacement of the former St Clement's surgery with no approved budget. The comment indicates this was due to unbudgeted archaeology works from a prior year that resulted in a budget shortfall the council had to cover.
findings.matters: Unbudgeted capital expenditure for heritage site archaeology indicates cost estimation or project management failures, and the council had to find cover for this shortfall outside the planned capital programme.
findings.figures: £91k actual expenditure with £0 approved budget
findings.quote: Unbudgeted expenditure for archaelogy works in prior year led to budget shortfall

findings.headline: Council budgeting £70,000 to address planning capacity issues during Local Government Reorganisation transition
findings.detail: Cabinet approved funding for a 24-month fixed term graduate planner post (£70,000 over 2027-28 and 2028-29) explicitly to support transition work and alleviate capacity issues within the planning service during LGR.
findings.matters: Explicitly flagged planning capacity issues during LGR suggest operational stress; capacity constraints in planning can delay income-generating development approvals and slow service delivery.
findings.figures: £70,000 over 2027/28 and 2028/29; 24-month fixed term position to be recruited in 2026-27
findings.quote: Approve a budget of £70,000 over 2027/28 and 2028/29, funded by the transitional reserve, to fund the final 18 months of a 24-month fixed term graduate planner position. This position will support transition work / alleviate capacity issues within the Planning service.

findings.headline: Council internally borrowing £68.3m and explicitly warns future external borrowing will be required
findings.detail: The General Fund holds zero external borrowing but £68.3m internal borrowing funded from cash reserves. The council states: as the capital financing requirement increases and cash reserves decrease, it will need to increase external borrowing.
findings.matters: Internal borrowing masks the true borrowing need and relies on maintaining high cash reserves; when reserves deplete, the council will need to access capital markets at rates and times not of its choosing.
findings.figures: Internal borrowing £68.333m; external borrowing £0 (General Fund); capital financing requirement £68.333m
findings.quote: While the council has sufficient cash and investment balances, it is able to internally borrow but as CFR increases, and cash and investment balances decrease, it will need to increase its external borrowing in addition to the £159.3m the council has already borrowed

findings.headline: Leisure centre utility costs exceeded budget; River Park overspend on utilities and maintenance
findings.detail: Leisure centre operations, particularly River Park Leisure Centre, experienced utility cost overruns driven by higher than forecast gas and electricity prices. River Park had a specific budget overspend on utility, security and maintenance.
findings.matters: Rising energy costs are eroding the net yield from leisure operations; sustained pressures may require service subsidy increases or revenue rises, affecting the council's financial headroom.
findings.figures: River Park £50,000 overspend on utilities, security and maintenance
findings.quote: Utility costs in relation to the leisure centres were higher than originally budgeted. This was due to higher gas and electricity prices.

findings.headline: Public conveniences refurbishment escalated to £194,000 from £80,000 budget; hidden structural defects discovered
findings.detail: Works at Houchin Street, Bishop's Waltham uncovered significant hidden liabilities in this conservation-area listed building, including roof timbers, handmade tiles, and lime rendering repairs. The council notes two further locations still require refurbishment and additional budget.
findings.matters: Escalating capital project costs and discovery of hidden liabilities in aging estate assets indicate weak pre-project due diligence; similar risks likely exist elsewhere in the council's property holdings.
findings.figures: £194,000 actual cost vs £80,000 original budget; two further locations identified as requiring refurbishment with additional budget needed
findings.quote: Once works commenced on the external repairs and the structure was opened up, it became clear that a significant amount of additional fabric repair was required. The building is a traditional period construction within a conservation area, and the works uncovered issues with roof timbers, handmade clay tiles, and areas requiring lime rendering.

findings.headline: Investment property portfolio fell £4.8m in fair value; no acquisitions from £4m strategic scheme
findings.detail: The council's investment property portfolio declined from £68.7m to £64.5m, including £4.822m in fair value losses and £1.463m in disposals. No acquisitions occurred despite a £4m Strategic Asset Purchase Scheme budget, as no suitable purchases were identified.
findings.matters: Declining property values reduce the capital base available for future schemes and restrict capital receipts funding; the absence of acquisitions despite significant available budget suggests weakening market conditions or deal availability.
findings.figures: Portfolio value £64.5m (down from £68.7m); fair value loss £4.822m; disposals £1.463m; net yield 3.85%
findings.quote: Property held for investment purposes in £000s 1 April 2025 68,735 ... Gains/(losses) in fair value (4,822) 31 March 2026 64,509

findings.headline: Business rates revaluation at Barfield Park & Ride created higher backdated liability
findings.detail: A Valuation Office review of the Barfield multi-storey park and ride determined a higher rateable value with backdated effect, resulting in a £327,000 adverse variance in 2025-26.
findings.matters: Retroactive property revaluations create unexpected liabilities and suggest the council's asset valuations and tax exposure forecasting may be incomplete.
findings.figures: £327,000 adverse variance
findings.quote: A review of business rates, by the valuation office, at the Barfield multi-storey park and ride, led to a higher and backdated business rates liability.

findings.headline: Council lost VAT relief on park and ride income; backdated HMRC payments accrued
findings.detail: The council had received a reduced VAT rate on park and ride income for years. On review, HMRC determined this relief was not applicable to councils. The council has accrued backdated payments as a result.
findings.matters: Retroactive regulatory interpretations create unexpected liabilities and demonstrate vulnerability to unforeseen tax rule changes affecting council income streams.
findings.figures: £616,000 adverse variance
findings.quote: The council had been in receipt of a reduced VAT rate for park and ride income for a number of years. On review this reduced VAT rate is no longer applicable to councils and so it has been removed and backdated payments to HMRC have been accrued for.

findings.headline: Business rates collection deficit of £3.3m driven by increased appeals provision
findings.detail: The council reported a £3.3m deficit on business rates collectable of almost £69m. The primary driver was a significant increase in the provision for appeals against rateable valuations.
findings.matters: A larger appeals provision indicates rising uncertainty about commercial property valuations; if a wave of successful appeals follows, budgeted business rates income could prove unachievable.
findings.figures: £3.3m deficit; total collectable business rates £69m
findings.quote: Business Rates – The total collectable business rates for 2025/26 were almost £69m within the year including significant ongoing and new reliefs. The outturn deficit of £3.3m related mainly to a significant increase in the appeals provision.

findings.headline: Council tax collection rate declined to 99.2%, creating a £2.9m collection fund deficit
findings.detail: The council forecast 99.3% collection in January 2025 but actual collection fell short, creating a £2.9m deficit. For 2026-27, the forecasted rate has been downwardly revised to 99.2%, reflecting this lower performance.
findings.matters: Collection rate declines represent direct revenue loss and signal deteriorating council tax compliance; sustained declines erode the reliable revenue base that underpins borrowing capacity.
findings.figures: £2.9m deficit; collection rate reduced from 99.3% forecast to 99.2% outturn
findings.quote: In January 2025, the Council forecast a collection rate of 99.3% based on previous experience of collection rates across the district. The outturn deficit of £2.9m reflected a reduction in the collection rate from 2024/25. The collection rate was reduced to 99.2% for 2026/27.

findings.headline: Reserves were drawn £636k more than budgeted
findings.detail: Budgeted reserve draw of £1.832m; actual draw £2.468m. The excess of £636k indicates the underlying position required more reserve support than forecast.
findings.matters: Reserve drawdown rates are key to assessing financial runway; drawing substantially more than planned signals tighter headroom than expected.
findings.figures: Budgeted £1.832m, Actual £2.468m
findings.quote: Reserve Related Movements -1.832 0.041 -2.468

findings.headline: Business rates collected £645k below budget
findings.detail: Budgeted retained business rates of £7.931m; actual outturn £7.286m. The shortfall of £645k represents an 8.1% variance from budget.
findings.matters: Business rates volatility is a material credit indicator; income shortfalls of this scale signal either market conditions or collection risk that affect sustainability.
findings.figures: Budget £7.931m, Outturn £7.286m
findings.quote: Retained Business Rates 7.931 7.931 7.286

findings.headline: Recreation Grounds & Open Spaces overspent by £14,870 on a £968,691 budget
findings.detail: The largest service in the town account overspent by 1.5%. Combined with cemetery overspend, this suggests grounds-maintenance cost pressures across the town services portfolio.
findings.matters: If grounds and facilities maintenance is running hot across multiple services, it may signal deferred backlog, material cost inflation, or staffing pressures that extend beyond the town account.
findings.figures: Forecast £968,691, outturn £983,561, variance (£14,870)
findings.quote: Recreation Grounds & Open Spaces 968,691 983,561 (14,870)

findings.headline: Cemetery services overspent by £31,552, reaching 35% above forecast
findings.detail: The cemetery service cost £122,751 against a forecast of £91,199. The variance is substantial and unexplained in this appendix. Cemetery provision is a recurrent service with a fixed budget; consistent overspends erode reserves.
findings.matters: Unexplained service overspends indicate either budget-setting misjudgement or uncontrolled cost pressure; repeated variances of this size force reserve drawdowns.
findings.figures: Forecast £91,199, outturn £122,751, variance (£31,552)

findings.headline: The paper states that the impact of local government reorganisation on the HRA is not yet known
findings.detail: The report says decision-making beyond September 2026 may be delayed if authorisations are required from the Secretary of State or the new organisation. It also says the business plan working balance has capacity to resource transition planning.
findings.matters: Decision delays and transition costs for an HRA during reorganisation are a governance point that finance directors at other councils going through the same process would track.
findings.figures: Decision-making risk beyond September 2026
findings.quote: The impact of local government reorganisation on the HRA specifically is not yet known.

findings.headline: Total HRA usable reserves and resources fell from £69.549m to £60.397m, with the Major Repairs Reserve down £7.136m
findings.detail: The Major Repairs Reserve fell from £34.119m to £26.983m and funded £18.110m of the capital programme. The 1-4-1 receipts balance fell from £5.462m to £4.817m, and shared ownership capital receipts were fully used, down from £0.909m to nil.
findings.matters: A fall of £9.152m in usable reserves in one year, mostly from the Major Repairs Reserve funding capital works, is the reserve draw-down a finance director would model against future programme needs.
findings.figures: £69.549m total at 31 March 2025; £60.397m total at 31 March 2026; £9.152m reduction; £34.119m to £26.983m Major Repairs Reserve; £18.110m MRR contribution to capital; £5.462m to £4.817m 1-4-1 receipts

findings.headline: 33 right-to-buy sales in 2025/26 were above the budget assumption, with external income £0.398m adverse
findings.detail: The report says the sales were significantly higher than the historic average and that the scheme changes made in late 2024/25 are expected to reduce future sales. RTB 1-4-1 receipts were £4.539m against a revised £8.884m, and the rest of the external income shortfall is attributed to higher void numbers.
findings.matters: Right-to-buy sales drive both rental income and 1-4-1 receipts, and a council reporting above-assumption sales with a forecast fall after scheme changes is a forecasting risk for any HRA.
findings.figures: 33 properties sold under right to buy in 2025/26; £0.398m adverse external income; £4.539m RTB 1-4-1 receipts against £8.884m revised budget; £4.345m variance on RTB 1-4-1 receipts
findings.quote: Thirty three properties were sold under right to buy in 2025/26, which is significantly higher than historic average and higher than the budget assumption

findings.headline: Average HRA cost of capital fell from 3.89% to 3.63%, with internal borrowing costs £0.608m lower than forecast
findings.detail: The report shows PWLB external debt rising by £4.768m to £159.259m while internal borrowing fell by the same amount to £53.341m. The capital financing requirement stayed at £212.6m. Interest receivable was £1.493m favourable because cash balances remained available to earn interest.
findings.matters: The split between PWLB debt and internal borrowing, and the rate the HRA pays on each, shows how the council is funding the capital programme without new borrowing against the CFR.
findings.figures: 3.89% average cost of capital in 2024/25 falling to 3.63%; £212.6m CFR; £159.259m PWLB external debt; £4.768m increase in PWLB debt; £53.341m internal borrowing; £0.608m lower internal borrowing cost; £1.493m favourable interest receivable
findings.quote: However, internal borrowing costs were lower than forecast by £0.608m, which is due to the interest payable on internal borrowing, and refinanced external borrowing, being lower than the budgeted 5%.

findings.headline: Premises costs were £2.1m adverse to budget, led by voids at £1.294m and responsive maintenance at £0.519m
findings.detail: The report links the voids overspend to 346 terminations in 2025/26 against 296 in 2024/25, a 17% increase, and to a higher cost per void. Responsive maintenance is attributed to more repairs, including damp and mould, and to repairs found through stock condition surveys being dealt with proactively.
findings.matters: Void cost per termination is a unit cost that a finance director benchmarks across a stock, and the paper ties its rise to both turnover and cost per void.
findings.figures: £2.1m premises adverse variance; £1.294m voids adverse; £0.519m responsive maintenance adverse; 346 terminations in 2025/26; 296 terminations in 2024/25; £7,770 to £8,815 average revenue cost per termination; 17% increase in terminations
findings.quote: The average revenue cost per termination also increased from £7,770 to £8,815.

findings.headline: Council awarded £1.297m of Local Authority Housing Fund round 4 funding for 2026/27 to 2028/29
findings.detail: The bid was submitted in February 2026. The report says match funding would come from the unallocated new build pot and that acquisitions will be considered case by case under delegated authority. In 2025/26 the unallocated new build budget of £6.434m recorded no outturn spend, and the majority of it is to be reprofiled to 2027/28.
findings.matters: External grant won against a bid, with match funding drawn from an unallocated capital pot, is the mechanism a finance director would look at when judging how much new-build capacity a grant actually unlocks.
findings.figures: £1.297m awarded between 2026/27 and 2028/29; £6.434m revised unallocated new build budget; £0 outturn on unallocated new build; £0.512m LAHF property acquisitions outturn
findings.quote: The Council was successful in its application, and £1.297m has been awarded between 2026/27 and 2028/29.

findings.headline: The £0.4m sewage treatment works budget covers three of four proposed nutrient-credit sites
findings.detail: Outline business cases went to the PAC board. Three sites will progress to final business case and further funding will be requested as those cases are developed. Nutrient credit sales of £0.292m in 2025/26 were transferred to earmarked reserves for future capital spend.
findings.matters: A nutrient-credit programme that generates income from new capital spend, but has a budget that does not cover feasibility-to-business-case costs for every site, is a funding gap a finance director at a neighbouring council facing similar requirements would weigh.
findings.figures: £0.4m original budget; four proposed sites reduced to three progressing; £0.292m nutrient credit sales in 2025/26; £0.240m sewage treatment works outturn; £1.586m revised budget
findings.quote: The original budget of £0.4m is not sufficient to proceed with the four proposed sites following initial feasibility work.

findings.headline: Kings Barton acquisitions spent £18.273m against a £20.000m revised budget, with 26 units completed in 2025/26
findings.detail: The report says a payment for units reaching 'golden brick' stage in March 2026 was made in early 2026/27, which created the £1.72m favourable variance and will be carried forward. A further 65 units are expected in 2026/27 and 55 in 2027/28.
findings.matters: A fixed unit schedule across three years, with payments tied to construction milestones, is the delivery profile a lender or a peer buying similar stock would check.
findings.figures: £18.273m outturn; £20.000m revised budget; £1.727m variance; 26 units completed in 2025/26; 65 units anticipated in 2026/27; 55 units expected in 2027/28
findings.quote: 26 units were completed during 2025/26, with a further 65 units anticipated in 2026/27 and the remaining 55 units expected to be completed in 2027/28.

findings.headline: Climate change emergency spend was £2.074m against a revised £5.336m after SHF Wave 3 funding was rescinded
findings.detail: The report attributes the delay to preparatory requirements on SHF Wave 3 and DESNZ holding battery installations. It says the funding was rescinded and the retrofit delivery strategy was redesigned with two pilot contractors. About 71% of stock is EPC-C or above, against a target of 82% for 2026/27 and 2027/28, and 36 properties were improved to EPC-C in 2025/26.
findings.matters: A grant rescinded mid-programme, followed by a redesigned delivery model against a 2030 EPC-C commitment, is a funding and delivery position that peers planning similar decarbonisation targets would compare.
findings.figures: £2.074m outturn; £5.336m revised budget; £3.262m favourable variance; approximately 71% of stock at EPC-C or above; 82% target; 36 properties improved to EPC-C in 2025/26; £6.400m 2026/27 revised budget
findings.quote: As a result of the above, and as outlined in the HRA budget report CAB3540, the SHF funding was rescinded, which took time and impacted on the construction contract programme of works.

findings.headline: Fire safety provision spent £0.781m against a revised £3.551m, with the underspend reprofiled across 2026/27 and 2027/28
findings.detail: The business plan allowed an additional £2m a year for three years for fire stopping and compartmentation. The report says 2025/26 focused on high-risk fire safety measures, mostly revenue repairs, and that the compartmentation programme started in Q4 with works at White Wings House. The 2026/27 revised budget for this line is £3.162m.
findings.matters: A three-year fire stopping programme whose first-year spend lands well below budget, with the balance moved into later years, is a timing risk a finance director would check against their own compartmentation schedule.
findings.figures: £0.781m outturn; £3.551m revised budget; £2.770m variance to revised; £2.7m favourable variance (para 11.26); £2m per annum for three years; £3.162m 2026/27 revised budget
findings.quote: The budget underspend will be reprofiled across 2026/27 and 2027/28.

findings.headline: HRA capital programme spent £28.585m in 2025/26 against a revised budget of £43.993m
findings.detail: Paragraph 2.2 puts the difference at £15.4m, with fire safety works, climate change and Kings Barton acquisitions named as the key movements since February. Appendices 3 and 4 revised budgets sum to £48.528m rather than the £43.993m total, and £3.535m is proposed for carry-forward into 2026/27.
findings.matters: A capital programme landing £15.4m below its revised budget, with the balance moved into later years, is a delivery-timing signal that a finance director here or at a peer council would want to check against their own plan.
findings.figures: £28.585m outturn; £43.993m revised budget; £15.4m lower than revised; £21.13m original budget; £3.535m carry-forward; £48.528m sum of revised budgets in Appendices 3 and 4
findings.quote: The Capital programme outturn was £28.585m against the revised budget of £43.993m agreed in the 2024/25 outturn report in September 2025.

findings.headline: HRA outturn for 2025/26 is a £2.262m deficit against a budgeted £2.030m deficit, reducing the working balance to £13.689m from £15.951m
findings.detail: The report states an adverse movement of £0.232m against budget. Paragraph 11.1 instead describes a surplus of £1.855m against a deficit budget of £1.704m, which does not match the £2.262m deficit in Appendices 1 and 2.
findings.matters: The HRA working balance is the statutory headroom the council must keep positive under s74 of the 1989 Act, so its movement is what a finance director here or at another council would track.
findings.figures: £2.262m deficit; £2.030m budgeted deficit; £0.232m adverse movement; £13.689m working balance; £15.951m opening balance at 31 March 2025; £1.855m surplus (para 11.1); £1.704m deficit budget (para 11.1)
findings.quote: The 2025/26 outturn was a deficit to the HRA of £2.262m for 2025/26, compared to the originally budgeted deficit of £2.030m; an adverse movement of £0.232m.

findings.headline: Demolition of the former River Park leisure centre is in the programme at £1,200k in 2027/28, subject to appraisal.
findings.detail: The demolition is listed in the subject-to-appraisal block with its full £1,200k in 2027/28, and sits under Healthy Communities. The paper does not say what replaces the building.
findings.matters: Disposal or demolition of a leisure facility on a council's own land is a capital and asset decision that other councils facing similar leisure-estate choices would track.
findings.quote: Demolition of former leisure centre at River Park Healthy Communities

findings.headline: The Guildhall capital improvements scheme is approved at £3,300k, with £2,800k falling in 2027/28.
findings.detail: The approved block shows £500k in 2026/27 and £2,800k in 2027/28 for Guildhall capital improvements, making it the largest single approved line in 2027/28 in the table.
findings.matters: A £2,800k single-year approved spend on a civic building concentrates cash outflow in 2027/28, which affects the council's cash and borrowing requirement in that year.
findings.quote: Guildhall capital improvements Thriving Places 500

findings.headline: CWR CIL-funded infrastructure works of £4,500k are subject to appraisal, phased over 2027/28 to 2029/30.
findings.detail: The scheme is funded from Community Infrastructure Levy and sits in the subject-to-appraisal block, with £1,000k in 2027/28 and £1,750k in each of 2028/29 and 2029/30 shown in the table.
findings.matters: Large CIL-funded infrastructure is a capital commitment whose funding depends on levy receipts and appraisal outcome, which finance officers at other councils with regeneration programmes would compare against their own.
findings.quote: CWR - CIL funded infrastructure works Thriving Places

findings.headline: The Strategic Asset Purchase Scheme carries a £4,000k unallocated budget in 2026/27, which the paper places under separate governance procedures.
findings.detail: SAPS is listed on its own line below the General Fund total, with its unallocated £4,000k shown in 2026/27 only. The paper says the scheme is governed separately as set out in the Capital Investment Strategy.
findings.matters: A £4,000k sum held outside the main programme totals, under a separate approval route, is a governance arrangement other finance officers and lenders would want to see the terms of.

findings.quote: The Strategic Asset Purchase Scheme (SAPS) is subject to separate governance procedures as outlined in the Capital Investment Strategy

findings.headline: The General Fund capital programme totals £46,123k over 2026/27 to 2035/36, of which £15,109k is classed as subject to appraisal and £31,014k as approved.
findings.detail: The programme is presented in two blocks, approved schemes and schemes subject to appraisal, with the appraisal block including projects starting in 2027/28 and later. The paper states that inclusion in the programme does not by itself authorise spending.
findings.matters: A finance director or lender can see how much of the ten-year programme is still awaiting appraisal and therefore not yet authorised, which bears on future borrowing and the reliability of the spending profile.

findings.quote: Total General Fund 14,861

findings.headline: Healthy Communities outturn £3,390k against a £2,935k budget, a £455k overspend.
findings.detail: The paper gives the Greener Faster, Good Homes for All, Thriving Places and Efficient and Effective outcomes alongside it. Good Homes for All shows an underspend of £1,094k against a £4,108k budget.
findings.matters: A service-level overspend shown against an underspend in another outcome area is the kind of variance finance officers compare when assessing budget control.

findings.quote: Healthy Communities 2,935 3,390 (455)

findings.headline: Funding of £25.2m, £1.1m above the original £24.1m budget, with the paper describing all of the additional funding as one-off in nature.
findings.detail: Retained business rates are available for general use. Other government grants, mainly new burdens, are for specific purposes such as homelessness and Homes for Ukraine. The paper lists £3.456m of specific support packages received or claimed in the year.
findings.matters: Funding that is described as one-off, alongside a specific-purpose grant mix, is a key consideration for councils planning ongoing baseline budgets.
findings.figures: £25.2m total funding; £24.1m original budget; £1.1m above budget; £3.456m specific support packages
findings.quote: In total, including Council Tax, funding of £25.2m was £1.1m higher than the original budget of £24.1m.

findings.headline: Net interest receivable £0.6m above budget, caused by higher than expected balances and higher than forecast rates of return.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the variance to higher balances, specifically s106 balances, and higher rates. Investment property income was £0.2m above budget because of unused contingencies for voids and rent reviews.
findings.matters: Interest income above forecast helped offset service pressures, and s106 balances held as cash are a recurring source of investment income for councils.
findings.figures: £0.6m additional net interest receivable; £0.2m additional investment property income; £0.1m adverse minimum revenue provision variance
findings.quote: Additional net interest receivable of £0.6m caused by higher than expected balances

findings.headline: Investment property portfolio valued at £64.5m at 31 March 2026, down from £68.7m at 31 March 2025.
findings.detail: The movement table shows a £4,822k loss in fair value during the year and £1,463k of disposals. The paper reports gross income of £4.04m and net income of £2.56m, an average net yield of 3.85%.
findings.matters: A fall in investment property valuation alongside disposals and a fair value loss is relevant to any council relying on commercial property income or holding a similar portfolio.
findings.figures: £64.5m valuation at 31 March 2026; £68.7m at 31 March 2025; £4,822k fair value loss; £1,463k disposals; £4.04m gross income; £2.56m net income; 3.85% average net yield
findings.quote: The council owns an investment property portfolio (assets held solely for rental income or capital appreciation) which was valued at £64.5m as at 31 March 2026 (£68.7m as at 31 March 2025)

findings.headline: General Fund financing costs of £2.2m in 2025/26, against a £1.9m forecast, equal to 8.7% of the net revenue stream.
findings.detail: The paper says financing costs were higher than forecast due to capital grant income used to fund prior-year unfinanced capital expenditure. The 2026/27 budget is £2.0m, equal to 7.7% of net revenue stream.
findings.matters: The proportion of net revenue stream absorbed by financing costs is a prudential indicator that lenders and finance directors track against affordability limits.
findings.figures: £2.2m actual; £1.9m forecast; 8.7% of net revenue stream; £2.0m 2026/27 budget; 7.7% 2026/27 proportion
findings.quote: The General Fund financing costs as a proportion of net revenue stream is higher than forecast

findings.headline: One-off revenue budgets outturn at £4.084m against a revised £7.763m, £3.679m below revised budget.
findings.detail: The original one-off budgets totalled £4.111m. The paper lists the largest carry-forwards, including Homes for Ukraine, Homelessness, Car Parks maintenance, Guildhall maintenance and Central Winchester Regeneration.
findings.matters: Large unspent one-off budgets carried forward signal how much project spend is deferred into the following year.
findings.figures: £4.084m outturn; £7.763m revised budget; £3.679m below revised budget; £4.111m original budget
findings.quote: The final outturn of £4.084m was therefore £3.679m below revised budget.

findings.headline: Major Investment Reserve transfer of £653,000, £1.1m below the February 2026 projection.
findings.detail: The shortfall against projection results from the transfers to the Property and Local Plan reserves. The paper describes the transfer as the balancing surplus.
findings.matters: A large reduction in the amount reaching the Major Investment Reserve shows how emerging pressures are competing with reserve-building in the same budget.
findings.figures: £653,000 transfer; £1.1m below February Cabinet projection
findings.quote: This is £1.1m less than the projections shown at February Cabinet (CAB3541) due to the above transfers to the Property and Local Plan reserves.

findings.headline: Public conveniences budget increased by £148,000 from capital receipts following condition surveys.
findings.detail: The increase covers three sites: Discovery Centre, Jewry Street; Station Road, Wickham; and Kidmore Lane, Denmead. The paper says the Town and Parish toilet works overspent because of the extent of fabric repairs found once work began.
findings.matters: Condition surveys finding structural costs after a scheme starts is a recognised risk for ageing public buildings in conservation areas.
findings.figures: £148,000 increase, funded by capital receipts; Discovery Centre total budget £50,000; Station Road £60,000; Kidmore Lane £50,000
findings.quote: an additional budget (including contingency) of £148,000, funded by capital receipts, has been added to the public conveniences budget following condition surveys

findings.headline: Food waste vehicles, containers and depot fit-out completed at £1.51m against a £1.8m total budget.
findings.detail: Food waste collection began in October 2025. The paper estimates the scheme could reduce the district's carbon footprint by 1,900 tonnes of CO2e per year.
findings.matters: A completed capital scheme delivered under its approved budget is a delivery outcome other councils with similar waste service changes can compare against.
findings.figures: £1.51m spent; £1.8m total budget; estimated 1,900 tonnes CO2e per year
findings.quote: The final spend represents a saving of just under £300,000.

findings.headline: No Strategic Asset Purchase Scheme acquisitions made from a £4m budget in 2025/26, as no suitable purchases were identified.
findings.detail: The S151 officer has delegated authority to acquire up to £4m following discussion with the SAPS Board, and acquisitions above £4m require Cabinet and Council approval. The paper states that no suitable purchases were identified during the year.
findings.matters: An unspent acquisition budget with a delegated approval route shows how a council's property investment pipeline is responding to market conditions.
findings.figures: £4m SAPS budget; £0 acquisitions in the year
findings.quote: During the financial year no suitable purchases were identified.

findings.headline: General Fund capital expenditure of £6.4m, against an original budget of £11.6m, excluding the SAPS scheme.
findings.detail: The paper compares outturn with the original budget, the September 2025 revised budget of £11.0m, and the February 2026 forecast of £9.9m. Further detail by project is given in Appendix 4.
findings.matters: A capital outturn well below original budget, with reprogramming between years, is a pattern finance directors monitor when judging delivery capacity.
findings.figures: £6.4m outturn; £11.6m original budget; £11.0m revised budget; £9.9m February 2026 forecast
findings.quote: General Fund capital expenditure amounted to £6.4m. Excluding the SAPS scheme (see below), this compares to an original budget of £11.6m, set in February 2025

findings.headline: Business rates collection outturn deficit of £3.3m, related mainly to an increase in the appeals provision.
findings.detail: Total collectable business rates for 2025/26 were almost £69m, including ongoing and new reliefs. The paper attributes the deficit mainly to the appeals provision.
findings.matters: Appeals provisions are a recurring pressure on business rates income and are relevant to any council carrying similar valuation risk.
findings.figures: £3.3m outturn deficit; almost £69m total collectable business rates
findings.quote: The outturn deficit of £3.3m related mainly to a significant increase in the appeals provision.

findings.headline: Council tax collection outturn deficit of £2.9m, with the paper noting a reduction in the collection rate from 2024/25.
findings.detail: In January 2025 the council forecast a 99.3% collection rate. The paper says the collection rate was reduced to 99.2% for 2026/27.
findings.matters: A collection fund deficit reduces the amount councils can rely on from council tax in future budgets, and is a direct signal for finance directors comparing collection performance.
findings.figures: £2.9m outturn deficit; 99.3% forecast collection rate; 99.2% collection rate for 2026/27
findings.quote: The outturn deficit of £2.9m reflected a reduction in the collection rate from 2024/25.

findings.headline: Park and ride VAT rate removed on review, with backdated payments to HMRC accrued, giving an income variance of £0.616m adverse.
findings.detail: The council had applied a reduced VAT rate to park and ride income for several years. On review the rate was found not to apply to councils, so the rate was removed and backdated amounts were accrued.
findings.matters: A VAT treatment error corrected through a backdated liability is a specific item other councils with similar income streams may need to check.
findings.figures: £0.616m adverse income variance (shown as -0.616 in the £m income variances table)
findings.quote: On review this reduced VAT rate is no longer applicable to councils and so it has been removed and backdated payments to HMRC have been accrued for.

findings.headline: General Fund earmarked reserve balances rose from £49.5m at April 2025 to £53.2m at March 2026.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the increase mainly to Community Infrastructure Levy receipts, new burdens funding held for 2026/27 spend, and general underspends transferred to reserves. The operational reserves balance rose from £14.2m to £15.0m, and the paper notes significant commitments against these balances.
findings.matters: A £3.7m rise in earmarked reserves in one year, alongside stated commitments against them, shows how much of a council's balance sheet is already committed to future spend.
findings.figures: £49.5m at April 2025; £53.2m at 31 March 2026; operational reserves £14.2m rising to £15.0m
findings.quote: General Fund earmarked reserve balances have increased from £49.5m at April 2025 to £53.2m at the end of March 2026.

findings.headline: General Fund 2025/26 outturn reports a favourable variance of £1.8m, with a budget surplus of £1,754,000 transferred to reserves.
findings.detail: The surplus is split between a Property reserve transfer of £601,000, a Local Plan reserve transfer of £500,000 and a Major Investment Reserve transfer of £653,000. The paper attributes the variance mainly to additional interest receivable, additional in-year government grants and net service variances.
findings.matters: It shows how a favourable year is being allocated across specific reserves rather than held in general balances, which is relevant to peers planning reserve use.
findings.figures: £1.8m favourable variance; £1,754,000 surplus; £601,000 Property reserve; £500,000 Local Plan reserve; £653,000 Major Investment Reserve
findings.quote: A final outturn favourable variance of just under £1.8m is reported

findings.headline: The Strategic Asset Purchase Scheme carries £4,000k of unallocated budget in 2026/27 and is governed separately under the Capital Investment Strategy.
findings.detail: A separate SAPS - unallocated line holds £4,000k in Thriving Places with no approved changes or reforecast. The paper notes that SAPS is subject to separate governance procedures.
findings.matters: Unallocated asset-purchase budget of this size, held outside the normal approval route, is something a lender or a finance director at a peer council would want to see when judging how much capital spending is still uncommitted.
findings.figures: £4,000k SAPS unallocated budget; £4,000k forecast
findings.quote: The Strategic Asset Purchase Scheme (SAPS) is subject to separate governance procedures as outlined in the Capital Investment Strategy

findings.headline: Chesil Multi Storey car park replacement lifts budget reduced from £500k to £350k following tender.
findings.detail: The original £500k budget for replacement lifts at the Chesil Multi Storey car park has been reduced by £150k to £350k after the tender process.
findings.matters: A tender that comes in below the budget reduces the capital needed for the scheme, which is a saving a finance director may want to compare with other procurements.
findings.figures: £500k original budget; £150k reduction; £350k forecast
findings.quote: Budget reduced following tender

findings.headline: Car Parks - various budget rises from £916k to £1,367k, including a £105k budget vired from revenue because the spend is capital in nature.
findings.detail: The car parks budget was increased by an approved change and a brought-forward balance. The comment says the budget was vired from revenue because the spend has been identified as capital in nature.
findings.matters: Moving spend from revenue to capital changes how it hits the council's accounts and borrowing requirement, and a finance officer at another council may face the same reclassification.
findings.figures: £916k original budget; £105k approved change; £346k brought forward; £1,367k forecast
findings.quote: Budget vired from revenue as spend identified as capital in nature

findings.headline: Revised 2026/27 General Fund capital programme forecast at £14,861k, against an original budget of £14,008k.
findings.detail: The original 2026/27 General Fund capital budget of £14,008k rose by £4,849k of approved changes and £2,758k brought forward from 2025/26. Other changes, including reforecasts, reduced it by £6,754k, giving the revised forecast.
findings.matters: The forecast sits £853k above the original budget even after £6,754k of reductions and reprofiling, which shows how far approved additions and brought-forward balances have pushed the year's programme beyond what was set in February.
findings.figures: £14,008k original budget; £4,849k approved changes; £2,758k brought forward from 2025/26; £(6,754)k other changes; £14,861k forecast
findings.quote: Total General Fund

findings.headline: Subject to Appraisal schemes fall by £6,250k in other changes, with the Brooks car park air handling and lighting budget of £1,000k now expected in 2027/28.
findings.detail: Other changes to the Subject to Appraisal section total £6,250k. Alongside the River Park demolition and the LEP bids, the CWR infrastructure works (£1,000k) were reprofiled to 2027/28, and the CWR bus and accessibility improvements (£250k) are now expected in 2027/28.
findings.matters: A £6,250k reduction in the uncommitted section of the programme shows the council moving spend into later years, which affects the timing of capital expenditure and the borrowing it will need.

findings.quote: Now expected in 2027/28

findings.detail: The original £2,000k budget for demolition of the former River Park leisure centre has been reprofiled to 2027/28 and reduced, leaving a nil forecast for 2026/27. The paper does not give the revised total budget.
findings.matters: Reprofiling a demolition scheme and cutting its budget after costings shows the council re-estimating a live project, and the total cost still has to be confirmed in a later year.

findings.quote: Reprofiled to 27/28 and budget reduced following costings

findings.detail: The LEP grant fund applications line sat under Subject to Appraisal with a £2,000k budget. The forecast is now nil and the comment reads that the bids were unsuccessful and the line was removed from the programme.
findings.matters: A grant-funded capital line removed after unsuccessful bids means the external funding the programme assumed will not arrive, so the council must either drop the scheme or find another funding source.
findings.figures: £2,000k original budget; £2,000k reduction; nil forecast
findings.quote: Bids unsuccesful - removed from programme

findings.headline: No Community Infrastructure Levy claim was made by Hampshire County Council in 2025/26 against a £664k budget
findings.detail: The CIL-funded HCC projects line has a £664k budget and nil actuals. Separately, the CIL-funded community projects line spent £494k of a £1,234k budget, with several external projects yet to start.
findings.matters: CIL receipts are a source of funding for infrastructure, and an unclaimed allocation shows income a council has not yet passed to a partner.

findings.quote: No claim from Hampshire County Council made in year

findings.detail: The unspent grant was transferred to the capital grants unapplied account rather than being lost. The paper records it as an underspend of grant funding carried forward.
findings.matters: Grant transferred to the unapplied account is held for future use, which affects a council's usable reserves and its future capital funding position.
findings.figures: Revised budget £1,528k; actuals £962k; under spend £566k
findings.quote: Underspent grant transferred to capital grants unapplied account

findings.headline: River Park Pavilion spent £1,844k against a £2,261k budget and was opened in May 2026
findings.detail: The paper records the pavilion as substantially complete and opened in May 2026. The scheme shows a £417k under spend against its revised budget.
findings.matters: A large leisure scheme delivered under its revised budget is a delivery record a finance officer at another council may want to compare with their own projects.
findings.figures: Revised budget £2,261k; actuals £1,844k; under spend £417k
findings.quote: Project substantially complete - opened in May 2026

findings.headline: The replacement of the former St Clement's surgery overspent by £91k, which the paper attributes to unbudgeted archaeology works in the prior year
findings.detail: The scheme has no 2025/26 budget and actuals of £91k, shown as an overspend. The paper gives the cause as unbudgeted prior-year expenditure on archaeology works. A separate £60k Chesil Theatre capital grant is also recorded as an overspend because revenue spend was reclassified as capital.
findings.matters: An unbudgeted cost carried into a later year shows how an archaeology or similar condition on a site can create a funding gap, and how a council records it.
findings.figures: St Clement's overspend £91k; Chesil Theatre capital grant overspend £60k
findings.quote: Unbudgeted expenditure for archaelogy works in prior year led to budget shortfall

findings.headline: Special maintenance vehicle replacements (£251k) and Meadowside solar PV (£60k) have moved into 2026/27
findings.detail: The paper records both schemes as not spent in 2025/26 and expected in the next financial year. The solar PV scheme is also shown in the General Fund table with a £60k budget and no actuals.
findings.matters: Schemes carried into the next year add to the 2026/27 capital programme that the council must fund and deliver.
findings.figures: Vehicle replacements £251k budget, nil actuals; Meadowside solar PV £60k budget, nil actuals
findings.quote: Expenditure now expected in 2026/27

findings.headline: £911k of provisional schemes 'subject to appraisal' had no spend in 2025/26, including £500k for energy management projects
findings.detail: The subject-to-appraisal block has an adjusted budget of £911k and no actuals. The paper says the £500k energy management budget was a provisional amount not required in the year.
findings.matters: Provisional capital budgets that go unspent in a year signal how far a council's capital plan is firm and how far it is aspirational.
findings.figures: Subject to appraisal adjusted budget £911k; actuals nil; energy management £500k
findings.quote: Provisional budget for energy management projects not required in year

findings.headline: The Strategic Asset Purchase Scheme's unallocated £4,000k had no spend in 2025/26, with the paper stating "No suitable purchases identified"
findings.detail: The £4,000k of unallocated SAPS budget shows no actuals in the year. The paper states the SAPS is subject to separate governance procedures under the Capital Investment Strategy.
findings.matters: A lender or finance officer tracking how much capital headroom a council holds for property purchases will see that the budget was not drawn in the year.
findings.figures: Unallocated budget £4,000k; actuals nil
findings.quote: No suitable purchases identified

findings.quote: This appendix details the revised budget approved in September 2025 (CAB3514), approved changes since then, and actual expenditure in 2025/26.

findings.headline: The Town Community Infrastructure Levy reserve closing balance is shown as £199,785 and £216,514, after an opening balance of £223,785.

findings.matters: The gap between the two closing balances and the percentage of net expenditure show how far the town's reserve cushion moved over the year, which a finance director comparing reserve adequacy at peer councils would look for.

findings.matters: Capital spend funded from a town reserve that comes in below the £110,000 figure is the kind of underspend a finance director at another council would compare against its own reserve-funded schemes.

findings.headline: Cemeteries spend is shown at £122,751 against £91,199, a variance of £31,552.
findings.detail: Cemeteries carries the largest single bracketed variance in the cost-of-services section. Recreation Grounds & Open Spaces shows a smaller bracketed variance of £14,870 on a £968,691 budget line.
findings.matters: A service line with the largest variance in a town account shows where in-year pressure sat, which a peer finance officer managing similar cemetery or open-space budgets would want to compare.

Cemeteries and Recreation Grounds & Open Spaces carry most of the bracketed variances, offset in part by Footway Lighting.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare how a small town-level cost base landed against its planned figure and which lines drove the difference.

findings.quote: Total Cost of Services 1,286,997 1,300,747 (13,750)

findings.matters: A finance director will want to know how the reserve position moved against budget, since reserve-related movements are one of the few ways a council can absorb an in-year pressure.

findings.matters: A large gap between the forecast and the final one-off spend shows how sensitive in-year reporting is to timing, which is a point finance officers elsewhere will want to test against their own forecasts.

findings.matters: Business rates are a volatile income stream, and a reduction against budget and forecast is a direct call on the council's reserves or savings to close the gap.
